title: Orthogonality, Projections, and Least Squares: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Orthogonality, Projections, and Least Squares: Visual Guide

1. When Ax Misses b | two sliders move b on and off the line Col(A) spans, flipping the panel between a solvable system and the nearest reachable point p with its error r | solvability was the end of the story before, and it is the starting line here: when b is outside the column space you stop demanding equality and take the closest point instead

2. The Shadow Formula | vector a is dragged around a fixed b = (4,3) while the worked arithmetic recomputes a.b, b.b, the vector projection, the scalar projection and the perpendicular leftover | you divide by the TARGET vector, b.b for the vector projection and |b| for the scalar one, and the shadow is the zero vector exactly when a.b = 0 while a negative dot product simply points it backwards

3. Closest Point Wins | a candidate q slides along the line beside a live plot of the distance |b - q| against t, with the angle between the residual and the line read out | the bottom of the distance curve and the 90-degree angle arrive at the same t, because "closest point" and "perpendicular residual" are one condition described twice

4. The Gram Matrix | the angle between two unit columns closes from 90 to 0 degrees while the table of pairwise dot products, the determinant and both condition numbers update | A^T A is invertible exactly when the columns are independent, and forming it squares the condition number so accuracy is lost in pairs

5. The Projection Matrix | three choices of A (a line, another line, an invertible 2x2) with b draggable, printing P built from A(A^T A)^-1 A^T alongside live idempotence and symmetry checks | one matrix depending only on A does the whole job, P is symmetric and idempotent so P p = p and P b = b inside the column space, and P collapses to the identity when A is square and invertible

6. Least Squares Residuals | three measurements are dragged up and down while the best-fit line, the vertical residuals, the normal equations and A^T r are recomputed | the residual is orthogonal to every column of A, so A^T r stays pinned at zero for every setting, which places r in the left null space N(A^T) and never in N(A)
